[folded GR-14.9.30.4-L2.1 = §14.9.30.4 21) d) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB342 LANDED. RULE (GR21, indexed rule d.1): 'If NEXT is specified or implied, the record to be made available is the first existing record in the physical file whose key of reference value is greater than or equal to the key value in the file position indicator.' VALIDATED: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "the first existing record in the physical file whose key of reference value is greater than or equal to the key value in the file position indicator" -> OK 21). WAS DIVERGES: the connector modelled the file position indicator as the PAIR (key value, arrival) - the arrival of whichever record the previous START happened to stop on - and ReadSequential's forward arm compared that pair. 14.9.41.4 GR17 e) 1. puts a KEY VALUE and nothing else in the indicator ('The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison', --check 14.9.41.4 -> OK 17)), which is exactly why rules e) and f) have to name 'the record that was made available by that prior READ statement' instead of consulting it. MEASURED before the fix (probe pb342a.cob; 01/PP 02/PP 03/PP released in that order): START F KEY IS NOT GREATER R-ALT with 'PP' searched in reverse, stopped on 03, and the following READ NEXT answered 03 and then at end - records 01 and 02 unreachable. NOW: ReadSequential branches on the previous operation. Under rule d) (_positioner 'S' or 'O') PositionCompare returns the KEY comparison alone, so the forward arm's c > 0 || c == 0 acceptance enters a duplicate set at its FIRST-released record, which is what GR26 makes 'first' mean going forward. Under rules e)/f) (_positioner 'R') the tie-break is the prior READ's record's release ordinal under the key of reference. The OPEN arm still takes seq[0] directly rather than comparing against an empty-string sentinel (correct under a 12.4.5.7 alphabet where SPACE weighs high). PINNED: conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/l1_start_dup_set_entry leg B (a REVERSE START into the PP set then READ NEXT delivers 03, 01, 02 - the whole set in release order) and conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_read_alt_dup_walk leg A.

[folded GR-14.9.30.4-L2.2 = §14.9.30.4 21) d) 2.: CONFORMS]

RULE (GR21, indexed rule d.2): 'If PREVIOUS is specified and the previous operation on the file was a START statement, the first existing record in the physical file whose key of reference value is less than or equal to the key value in the file position indicator.' WAS DIVERGES: Start stored _fpiKey AND _fpiArrival, and the reverse arm compared the pair, so a FORWARD START into a duplicate set left the position on the FIRST-released record and READ PREVIOUS handed that same record back, leaving the rest of the set unreachable in reverse. The earlier adjudication had noticed the modelling error and closed with 'no divergence was demonstrable'; the construct that demonstrates it is one START and one READ. MEASURED before the fix (probe pb342a.cob; 01/PP 02/PP 03/PP released in that order): START F KEY IS NOT LESS R-ALT with 'PP' then READ PREVIOUS answered 01 and then at end. NOW Start records the KEY VALUE alone (14.9.41.4 GR17 e) 1.), so under rule d) the reverse arm scans the ordered sequence from the end and accepts the first record whose key is <= the indicator - inside a duplicate set that is the LAST-released record, which is what GR26's 'in the case of PREVIOUS, in the reverse order' makes 'first' mean going backward. StartFirstLast records a key value on the same footing (GR18/GR19). PINNED: conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/l1_start_dup_set_entry leg A (a FORWARD START into the PP set then READ PREVIOUS delivers 02, 01, 03 - the whole set in reverse release order, with the 14.9.30.4 GR27 b) '02' statuses) and conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_read_alt_dup_walk leg B.
